title: Spouses' Joint House and Land: Is Registering One Name a Problem?
desc: Whose name goes on the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) for joint property, can one name sell or mortgage alone, and what happens on divorce or death.
summary: What spouses need to know when a house and land are joint property: names on the certificate, who may sign to sell or mortgage, dividing joint property and the estate when one spouse dies.
body: p

Many couples buy a home but the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) shows only the husband's or only the wife's name. This article summarizes provisions of the Civil Code 2015 and the Land Law 2024 relating to a house and land that are spouses' joint property.
p

Note on scope: determining whether a house is joint or separate property (bought before or after the wedding, separately gifted, separately inherited, a property regime agreement, etc.) is governed by the Law on Marriage and Family – this document is not yet in our library, so this article does not go into that part.
h2
1. What is spouses' joint ownership?
p
Under Article 213 of the Civil Code:
ul
Spouses' joint ownership is divisible consolidated joint ownership, meaning each person's share is not determined in advance (Article 210).
Spouses have equal rights in possessing, using and disposing of the joint property.
Spouses may agree or authorize each other to possess, use and dispose of the joint property.
Joint property may be divided by agreement or by decision of the Court.
If the spouses choose a property regime by agreement under the law on marriage and family, that regime applies.
h2
2. Whose name must the certificate show?
p

Under Clause 4, Article 135 of the Land Law 2024, a house and land that are the spouses' joint property must show the full names of both the wife and the husband on the certificate, unless the spouses agree to record one person's name as representative.
p
A certificate issued earlier showing only the wife's or husband's name is reissued to show both names upon request.
h2
3. Can one named person sell or mortgage alone?
p

Having one name on the certificate does not take away the rights of the other person if the house and land are joint property. Disposal of consolidated joint property is carried out by agreement of the co-owners or as provided by law (Clause 2, Article 218). In practice, when selling, giving or mortgaging a house and land that are joint property, both spouses sign together, or one signs with a power of attorney from the other.
p

A contract to transfer, give or mortgage a house and land must be notarized or certified (Point a, Clause 3, Article 27 of the Land Law). A buyer should ask the seller to prove the status of the property to avoid the contract being disputed later.
h2
4. A house and land shared by the whole family
p

If the house and land were contributed to and created by family members together, then disposal of the real estate requires the agreement of all adult family members with full civil act capacity, unless the law provides otherwise (Article 212). A household's land plot is issued one certificate stating the full names of the members who share the land use right (Clause 5, Article 135 of the Land Law).
h2
5. On divorce or when one spouse dies
ul

Divorce: joint property is divided by agreement or by decision of the Court (Clause 4, Article 213). Real estate divided between spouses on divorce by agreement or by a Court ruling is exempt from personal income tax (Clause 2, Article 18 of Decree 253/2026/ND-CP).

When one spouse dies: only the deceased's share of the joint property is the estate (Article 612); this share is divided by will or by law, and the surviving spouse both keeps their own share and is a first-rank heir (Article 651).
h2
6. Advice for spouses
ol
When registering the certificate, record both names if it is joint property; if an old certificate has one name, carry out the reissuance procedure.
If you agree that one person's name will represent both, make a clear written agreement and keep it safe.
Keep documents proving the source of funds for the purchase (separate gift, separate inheritance, etc.) if you want it treated as separate property.
When selling or mortgaging, prepare the signatures of both or a notarized power of attorney.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace legal documents. The grounds for determining joint and separate property and dividing property on divorce are provided by the Law on Marriage and Family – this document is not yet in our library. The Land Law 2024 is partially no longer in force. In case of a dispute, consult a lawyer or a notary.
